# S2.9 Isolate e2e specs that race on shared stored state

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Parent | S2 |
| Role | IMPLEMENTATION |
| Level | L1 |
| Contracts | C-ISO@1, C-SETTINGS@1 |
| Depends | S2.8 |
| Findings | none |
| Confidence | reproduced twice, independently, at the base commit as well as on S2.8 — `docs/v2/state/reviews/S2.8-impl.md:68-108` and `docs/v2/state/returns/S2.8.md:50-74` |

## Objective

The e2e line at **default workers** exits 0, N times in a row, so S2.R's
borrowed S2.8 V3 row passes as written.

Every failure recorded against that row is a race between specs over **stored
state**, not over product behaviour: the single `theme` row in
`GET/PUT /api/settings`, and the number of rows in `GET /api/formats`. The
suite runs `fullyParallel: true` (`e2e/playwright.config.ts:85`) against one
server and one data folder, so a spec that writes a global row and a spec that
reads it can be in flight at the same moment. S2.8's reviewer ran the literal
row four times and got **exit 1 on runs 1–3 and exit 0 on run 4**
(`S2.8-impl.md:68-74`), on a different failing spec pair each time; S2.8's
implementer got exit 1 on 3 of 3 with the change and 2 of 3 **at base
`f4c7696`** with the change reverted (`returns/S2.8.md:50-74`). The owner
accepted V3 on the serial run under **AM-086** and authorised this card in the
same amendment.

This card changes the tests' isolation and nothing else.

## Must not edit
- **Any production code.** Not `web/`, not `server/`, not `shared/`, not
  `src-tauri/`. There is no product defect here: the API is a correct
  single-global-row API and the tests are wrong about owning it. A change to
  `server/src/routes/settings.ts` or `server/src/db/settings.ts` would be a
  behaviour change this card has no authorisation for (Stop condition 5).
- `e2e/playwright.config.ts`, in particular **not** `:88`. Setting `workers: 1`
  unconditionally, or moving the CI-only spread to always apply, is the
  tempting one-line fix and it is exactly the thing this card exists to refuse:
  it trades a four-worker suite for a one-worker suite to hide a test-isolation
  bug, and it makes every future row slower while proving nothing. The pass
  condition in Verification is **default workers**.
- `e2e/support/no-english.ts`, and in particular **not** the
  `checkVisibility({ checkOpacity: true })` call at `:138`. Narrowing it, or
  dropping `checkOpacity`, is the tempting wrong fix for a flaky Spanish screen
  and it re-admits the leak S2.6 exists to catch (NEXT-SESSION "Do not"). The
  sanctioned answer to AM-076's staggered-entrance flake is to wait the screen
  out, which `arrivedStrings` at `:187-195` already does.
- No skip, no `test.fixme`, no `test.slow`, no `test.describe.configure({ mode:
  'serial' })` added as a **whole-file** blanket over a spec that does not
  need it, no retry, no `expect.poll` timeout inflation, and no assertion
  deleted. All of these are Stop conditions below, not options.
- `docs/v2/evidence/P2.2/screenshots/*.png` — **never committed and never
  edited**. Any `npm run e2e` rewrites them at sizes that contradict
  `evidence/P2.2/v1-e2e.md:184-187`, which is routine and is reverted with
  `git checkout -- docs/v2/evidence/P2.2/screenshots/` after every run (V4).
- Checkpoint and plan state: `docs/v2/state/cards/S2.9.json` is coordinator-owned
  — read it if it exists, never write, edit, delete or create it. Likewise
  `state/PROGRESS.json`, `state/AMENDMENTS.md`, `state/NEXT-SESSION.md`,
  `state/dispatch/*` and every other card file.
- No threshold, no guard, no contract, no dependency edge and no
  `CONTRACTS.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `RUN-CONFIG.md`, `TRACEABILITY.md`,

- `prototype/`, and the whole checkout outside the files above.

## Fixed decisions
1. **The fix is isolation, and it is chosen per race.** Two shapes are
   sanctioned and both are the repo's own: **(a)** a per-test save/restore of
   the contested row, exactly as `brand.spec.ts:301-333` does it and as the
   `storedLanguage` auto-fixture at `support/fixtures.ts:42-55` does it for the
   stored language; and **(b)** `test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' })` on
   **only the describe block or test that writes the contested row**, never on a
   whole file that does not need it. Where one row is read and written by
   **different files** — the theme row is read by `settings-appearance.spec.ts`
   and written by both it and `workspace.spec.ts:553` — (a) and (b) alone are
   not enough, because Playwright's `serial` mode orders tests **within** a
   file or block and does not stop another worker entering the same row at the
   same moment. In that case the sanctioned addition is a **narrow lock around
   the appearance tests only**, in `support/fixtures.ts`, held for **the window
   that touches the row** — from the write to the last assertion that reads it
   back, and nothing else — and taken by every test and every hook that writes
   or asserts the theme row, and by nothing else in the suite. The suite keeps
   its default workers and its wall-clock. A lock the whole suite would have to
   take is not a lock, it is `workers: 1` with extra steps.

   **That lock is cross-process, and it must be.** Playwright runs each test in
   a worker **process**, and with `fullyParallel: true`
   (`e2e/playwright.config.ts:85`) and a `--repeat-each` amplification it
   deliberately spreads repeats across workers — so the tests that must
   serialise are routinely in three or four different processes at once. An
   in-memory mutex in `support/fixtures.ts` therefore coordinates **nothing**: a
   module-level `let tail = Promise.resolve()`, a `Map` of in-flight keys, a
   class with a `static` flag, or any other promise chain in one process is not
   a lock here. It fails V1 with the very race this card removes, and the
   obvious next move after that — `e2e/playwright.config.ts:88` — is Stop
   condition 2. The sanctioned shape is a **lock file**, and these six points
   are the fix, not suggestions:

   - **Path.** Under `APUNTA_DATA_DIR`, which is this run's sandbox data
     directory and is already in the environment of every worker
     (`e2e/playwright.config.ts:13`). One key, one path, e.g.
     `<APUNTA_DATA_DIR>/appearance.lock`. It is therefore inside the sandbox
     run folder (C-ISO@1 rule 1) and inside nothing else, exactly as
     `brand.spec.ts:61-62` claims for the data directory.
   - **Acquisition is atomic.** `fs.mkdirSync(path)` or
     `fs.openSync(path, 'wx')` — an operation that either creates or fails with
     `EEXIST`. Never a read-then-write, never an `existsSync` probe followed by
     a create, both of which have the window this card exists to close.
   - **Bounded retry, with the number.** Poll on a short fixed interval against
     a deadline of **20 s**, and fail the waiting test with a named message —
     the elapsed wait, the deadline, and which worker holds the file — when the
     deadline passes. An unbounded wait is a hang wearing a lock's clothes. 20 s
     is not a round number picked for looks: it is derived in the next bullet,
     and it sits **below** Playwright's default test timeout on purpose, so a
     queue longer than the budget ends with this card's own message instead of
     as `Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded`, which is indistinguishable from a
     hung web server and invites exactly the remedies Must not edit closes.
   - **The hold's width, and what it costs — the arithmetic.**
     `e2e/playwright.config.ts` sets no test `timeout` (its only two are the
     `webServer` ones at `:127` and `:139`), so every test runs under
     Playwright's default of 30 000 ms (`playwright/lib/common/index.js:524`,
     `var defaultTimeout = 3e4`) and a fixture's wait is charged to that budget.
     Two things follow, and both are why the wait fits without `test.slow()` and
     without a timeout. First, the hold is the row-touching window above, never
     the whole test body. Second, the queue is bounded by the **worker count,
     not the repeat count**: Playwright runs at most `W` tests at once, so at
     most `W − 1` are ever waiting on the lock and the worst wait is
     `(W − 1) × H`, where `H` is the longest hold. In V1, `W = 4`
     (`--workers=4`) and `H` is capped at **6 s**, so `W × H = 24 s ≤ 30 s`:
     worst wait `3 × 6 = 18 s`, plus the holder's own 6 s, leaves 6 s for setup
     and teardown — `18 s < 20 s < 24 s < 30 s`. The `--repeat-each=3` is
     absent from that arithmetic deliberately: V1's 24 acquisitions (8
     lock-takers × 3) recycle through a queue three deep as workers free up,
     and 24 *serialised whole-test* holds would be testing the lock's queue
     rather than the race — the same reasoning that excludes
     `formats.spec.ts` from the amplification in decision 2. Measure `H` at V1
     (the longest of the five `brand.spec.ts` tests, whose window is nearly the
     whole test because the PUT is inside `openHome` at `:187` and
     `assertPainted` reads back what it wrote) and record it in the return file
     with the inequality it was checked against; at V3, check the same
     inequality against the workers actually in force, where the same eight
     tests run once per project (`e2e/playwright.config.ts:108-113`) — that
     doubles the acquisitions, not the queue — and where CI's `W = 1` (`:88`)
     means no queue at all, which is the same fact that makes a CI green no
     evidence (Read). **A measured `H` over the cap is a finding, not a
     licence.** The one sanctioned response is to narrow a hold by moving work
     that cannot observe the row outside it: the two `checkScreen` scans at
     `settings-appearance.spec.ts:41` and `:52` are the obvious candidates,
     because they read the DOM and never the stored theme, and moving one
     deletes no assertion and weakens none. Past that, record both numbers and
     report it as a new finding in the shape of decision 4's escalation.
     Raising the deadline, `test.slow()`, a retry, or anything in
     `e2e/playwright.config.ts` are not responses to it.
   - **Release in teardown**, removing the file it created, so a test that
     fails or throws cannot deadlock the rest of the run. Teardown releases the
     same path setup took, and only the holder releases it. For the
     caller-managed pair in the last bullet, teardown is a `finally` around the
     window (and the `afterAll`'s own release sits after its assertions, never
     before).
   - **Explicitly requested, never `{ auto: true }`.** The lock is taken only
     where it is asked for by name, and nowhere else, because an `auto` fixture
     is taken by *every* test in the suite and the paragraph above says in so
     many words that "nothing else in the suite does". It is requested by **every
     writer and every asserter of that row, in a test or in a hook**: the two
     tests in `settings-appearance.spec.ts:21` and `:77`, the one at
     `workspace.spec.ts:548`, the five in `brand.spec.ts` at `:335`, `:343`,
     `:351`, `:359` and `:398`, **and the describe's own `beforeAll`/`afterAll`
     pair at `brand.spec.ts:301-311` and `:313-333`**, which read the row and
     `PUT /api/settings` back at `:315`. That hook pair is a writer like any
     other, and the sharpest one: in an amplified run it restores whatever the
     row said when the describe started, which is a *different* value from the
     one a sibling is asserting, and a test-scoped fixture cannot reach a hook.
     The sanctioned shape is therefore a small exported `acquire`/`release`
     pair in `support/fixtures.ts` that each hook calls around **its own**
     read or restore window (two short holds, never one spanning the
     serial describe, whose five navigations and screenshots would break the
     `H` cap) and that a test may call directly for its own window. **The lock
     is not re-entrant and is never nested:** no caller acquires while it or
     its describe's hook already holds it, so a test inside `brand.spec.ts`'s
     describe is never waiting on its own `beforeAll` (AM-090) — still "a new
     isolation helper … added beside the existing ones", so inside May edit.
     Eight tests and one hook pair: that is the whole set, on the same evidence
     the first review recorded (IR-01) — the theme row is written or asserted
     in `brand.spec.ts`, `settings-appearance.spec.ts` and
     `workspace.spec.ts:553`, and nowhere else in `e2e/`.
2. **The formats race is fixed by scoping the assertion, never by weakening
   it.** `formats.spec.ts:56`'s `expect(formats).toHaveLength(before + 1)`
   reads a **global** count and is therefore unanswerable while a sibling
   worker POSTs a format. The fix is to assert the same proposition about the
   rows this test can be responsible for, and it has three parts, of which the
   first is the one that makes the other two work:

   - **`before` itself becomes the scoped count.** The read at `:39-40` stops
     counting `formats.length` and counts only the rows in scope, so
     `before + 1` is arithmetic on a number this test can be responsible for.
     Keeping the global read while scoping only the assertion is a fix that
     still fails, because the global `before` is the flaky reading and it
     would still be one of the two operands.
   - **The rows in scope are this test's standard progress note, and it takes
     two conditions to name them**: `name === 'Progress note'` **and** the
     seven section names asserted at `:66-74`. The name alone is not enough —
     `workspace.spec.ts:406-408` also POSTs a format named `Progress note`,
     with four sections, and it is a sibling of this test in a default-worker
     run. The second condition keeps that row out of both `before` and the
     after-count, so no sibling outside this file can move the number. There is
     no need to touch that test.
   - **`created` is identified the same way**, as the one row present after
     and absent before — compared by `id`, since the ordering that
     `formats.at(-1)` at `:57` relies on is exactly the ordering a sibling
     breaks. The assertions at `:65-75` are then made against that row
     unchanged and unweakened.

   The result is **strictly stronger** than the global count: it cannot be
   satisfied by an unrelated sibling's row. Deleting the count assertion, or
   replacing it with `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual`, is not the fix and is Stop
   condition 3.

   **What scoping does not cover, and what V1 therefore does.** Scoping answers
   interference from *other specs*. It does not answer interference from
   **another copy of the same test**, and this test cannot make its own rows
   distinguishable: the name is not the test's to choose, because the row is
   created by the onboarding card at `:49` and named by the server, which is
   what `:65` asserts. Three concurrent repeats of `formats.spec.ts:33` would
   each read `before = 0`, each create one row in scope, and each see two.
   Scoping by a per-test unique name is therefore not available here, and
   **V1 runs `formats.spec.ts` at `--repeat-each=1`, excluded from the
   amplification** — stated here, with its reason, rather than left to be
   discovered as an unexplained `before + 1` failure. The amplification is not
   dropped, it is aimed: `--repeat-each=3` stays on the four theme racers,
   which is where the overlap window this card is about actually lives, and
   `formats.spec.ts` still runs once per run inside V3's five whole-suite
   passes, where the scoped count is what makes that single instance
   dependable. The exclusion is a scheduling choice, not a licence to weaken
   the assertion, and it does not reach `retries` (`:87`), which stays put.
3. **Nothing is skipped, retried or weakened to get the row green.**
   `retries` stays at its config value (`:87`, zero outside CI) and V3's pass
   condition is **five consecutive exit-0 runs at default workers**, not one
   green run with a retry behind it. In CI `retries: 2` would mask a race that
   this card exists to remove, so a CI-only green is not evidence and must not be
   quoted as one.
4. **The flake at `settings-appearance.spec.ts:64-65` is part of this card, and
   it is the same root cause.** Those two assertions re-read the theme after a
   reload, and the reload is a window in which a sibling's PUT lands — the same
   shared row as the recorded races, not a separate animation or timing defect.
   It is fixed by decisions 1 and 2 and is proved fixed by V1 and V3. If after
   those changes `:63-65` still flakes, that is a **new finding for the
   coordinator**, reported with the run it was seen in — and it is emphatically
   not a licence to touch `no-english.ts` or to inflate a timeout (Must not
   edit; NEXT-SESSION's residual on AM-076 says what a future flake there is
   and is not).
5. **`plan.spec.ts:58` needs no isolation, and the reason is the finding, not a
   shrug.** The review saw it fail once and did not capture the assertion
   (`S2.8-impl.md:95-97`), and its `:21` citation is not a test — see Stop
   condition 4. Its setup does write shared state (`:70-79`), so the question
   is whether any other spec can *observe* it, and the answer is no, on three
   counts read off the code. The format it POSTs is named
   `uniqueName('E2E plan format')` at `:70`, so it is a row no other test
   creates and no assertion counts: the suite's only global format count is
   `formats.spec.ts:56`, and decision 2 scopes **both** of its operands to
   `name === 'Progress note'` plus the seven section names, which this row is
   not. The patient at `:73` is `uniqueName('E2E Plan Patient')` and the three
   notes at `:75-79` hang under it, so they are reachable only through that
   test's own `?patient=` link — nothing in the suite enumerates patients or
   notes globally. And it never reads or writes the theme row, so decision 1's
   lock is not for it: "nothing else in the suite does" stands, and a request
   there would serialise a test that touches no contested state and take a
   place in the queue decision 1's arithmetic just sized. **Its change is
   therefore none**, and "its change is none" is the finding to write down in
   the return file, not an instruction left undone. If it fails at V1 or V3 for
   a reason its own code does not explain, that is Stop condition 4 unchanged;
   inventing a fix for an uncaptured failure is how a test becomes a false
   promise.
6. **The evidence of the fix is repetition, at default workers, on the whole
   suite.** V3 runs the RUN-CONFIG §3 e2e line five consecutive times, in one
   sandbox run, with nothing between the runs but the screenshot restore. The
   expected result is **exit 0 five times out of five**, with the suite's passed
   and skipped counts recorded from every run. The tripwire is the repetition:
   a card that reports one green run has not shown what it was asked to show,
   and the base fails this row on 2 of 3 and 3 of 4 runs respectively
   (`returns/S2.8.md:50-57`, `S2.8-impl.md:68-74`) — so a single run is
   indistinguishable from the flake it is meant to have fixed.
7. **The serial invocation is not the pass condition.** `npx playwright test
   --workers=1` from `e2e/` is how the green serial evidence in S2.8 was
   obtained, and `npm run e2e -- --workers=1` **silently drops the flag** (npm
   warns `Unknown cli config "--workers"` and runs default workers anyway —
   `S2.8-impl.md:76-80`, finding 2). Either form may be run **in addition** to
   V3 to narrow a failure down; neither may be reported as V3, and a report that
   only contains a serial run is `FAIL` on this card's row as written.
8. **The card is L1 and offline.** It edits test files only, changes no
   production code, needs no new build of its own, no model, no vendor and no
   acquisition. It does start servers, exactly as the L1 cards P2.2, P3.2, P4.1
   and S2.1 do, so the dispatch assigns a port from 7800 to 7889, every launch
   goes through `scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs` (C-ISO@1), and **7717 is never
   contacted**. `npm run e2e` builds the app and starts both servers itself
   (`e2e/playwright.config.ts:115-142`), and **one** `sandbox.mjs env` is
   therefore the whole arrangement: the es-MX server takes `7852 + 1` and
   `<runFolder>/data-es-MX` on its own (`:32-36`), both inside the same run
   folder. Do not run a second `env --port` for it —
   `printEnv` (`scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs:299-310`) exports no
   `APUNTA_E2E_ES_PORT` and no `APUNTA_E2E_ES_DATA_DIR`, so it cannot supply
   what that server reads; and sourcing a second env **after** the first
   overwrites `APUNTA_E2E_PORT` and `APUNTA_DATA_DIR`, which moves the
   *English* server onto the second port and its data folder, leaving `7852`
   unused. This is the trap S2.6 filed at `reviews/S2.6-ir.md:290-322` and
   settled at `reviews/S2.6-postUI-ir.md:54`, where a second env is "the
   documented alternative, not a requirement". Playwright's browsers are **not**
   in `docs/v2/ACQUISITION.md`, so `npx playwright install` is not run; this box
   uses the config's own documented escape hatch,
   `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE=/usr/bin/chromium` (`:57-61`), which is an
   addition to the row's command and not a substitution for it. Nothing is
   downloaded (HS-3).
9. **The May-edit list is this list and no wider.** A discoverable second race —
   a new spec writing the theme row, or a seventh spec asserting a global count
   — is a **finding to report**, not a licence to add that file here (§6
   reserves widening to the owner; AM-086 authorised this card's scope
   specifically). Report the path, the line, and what would need isolating, and
   stop if the fix cannot be made without opening it.

## Steps
1. Confirm the base and the tripwire **before** editing anything: run the
   RUN-CONFIG §3 e2e line three times at default workers in a sandbox env, with
   `PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE` exported, and record each run's exit code,
   failing spec files and line numbers, and passed/skipped counts. The
   expectation is that **at least one of the three fails** (base evidence: 3 of 4
   and 2 of 3). If all three pass, that is not a licence to do nothing — it is
   Stop condition 1, because the card would have no reproduction to fix and its
   green would be luck. Restore the P2.2 screenshots after each run.
2. Apply decision 1 to the theme row: the save/restore and/or the narrow
   **cross-process file lock** in `support/fixtures.ts`, explicitly requested by
   the eight tests that write or assert it —
   `settings-appearance.spec.ts:21` and `:77`, `workspace.spec.ts:548`, and the
   five in `brand.spec.ts` at `:335`, `:343`, `:351`, `:359` and `:398` — and
   by the `brand.spec.ts` `beforeAll`/`afterAll` pair at `:301-333`, through the
   exported `acquire`/`release` pair, held only for the row-touching window and
   never past it — for the hook pair, one short hold in `beforeAll` around the
   read and one in `afterAll` around the restore, never one spanning the
   describe, and never nested with a test's own hold (AM-090). Apply decision 2 to `formats.spec.ts`: scope the read at
   `:39-40` as well as the count at `:56`, and identify `created` by `id` rather
   than by position. Apply decision 5's finding to `plan.spec.ts:58`: it needs
   no isolation and no edit, and the reason it needs none goes in the return
   file. Change nothing else in those files: not the fixtures, not
   `checkScreen` calls, not the `NOTES`/`SOAP` constants, not the comments that
   explain what a test is for.
3. Run V1 — the amplified, targeted repetition over the racing files, with
   `formats.spec.ts` at `--repeat-each=1` (decision 2). This is cheap and it
   localises, so it goes before the whole suite.
4. Run V2 — the L1 gate and the changed-path check.
5. Run V3 **last and uninterrupted**: five consecutive default-worker runs of the
   RUN-CONFIG §3 e2e line in one sandbox, restoring the P2.2 screenshots between
   runs and not touching the tree between them. Write each run's command, exit
   code, start and end time and output excerpt into `docs/v2/evidence/S2.9/`
   with sandbox paths written `<sandbox>` and the home folder `~` (RUN-CONFIG
   §4), and record in the return file: the base runs from Step 1, the
   per-file change you made and why that shape, the five exit codes with their
   passed/skipped counts, and — if any run failed — the failing spec and line
   verbatim rather than a summary. Then V4. Leave everything uncommitted for the
   coordinator.

## Why this is a new card, and not an amendment

Recorded so the next reader does not repeat the detour.

- **Not an amendment to S2.8.** Its May edit is `shared/src/i18n/es-MX.ts` and
  `docs/v2/evidence/S2.8/responses.md` (`S2.8.md:19-23`); it cannot open an
  `e2e/tests/*.spec.ts` file, and it is `APPROVED`
  (`docs/v2/state/PROGRESS.json`), which is not a thing an amendment can act on.
- **Not a change to S2.8's V3 row.** AM-086 accepted V3 on the serial run and
  **changed no row text and no threshold**; rewriting an acceptance row is the
  owner's, per §6 and NEXT-SESSION's residual on V1's wording. This card leaves
  the row exactly as written and makes the tree pass it.
- **Not S2.9 folded into S2.R.** S2.R is the parent review and its V3 is S2.8's
  borrowed e2e row. Folding this work into the review would mean the review
  edits test files, which is a review's job nowhere in this plan, and it would
  put a fix and an acceptance in one attempt.
- So: a new card, **S2.9**, parent S2, depending on **S2.8**, and therefore
  picked up automatically by **S2.R** — a parent review's `Depends` is generated
  from its child list (`docs/v2/tools/plan-lib.mjs:parseMilestones`), so no
  hand-edited edge is needed, and `docs/v2/DEPENDENCIES.md` is regenerated by
  `node docs/v2/tools/check-plan.mjs` rather than edited. It is placed before
  S2.R for the reason AM-086 gives: S2.R borrows S2.8's V3, which would otherwise
  fail the same way.

## Stop conditions
1. **The three base runs all pass.** Stop and report, with the counts. There is
   no reproduction to fix, the card's premise cannot be shown on this box, and
   a change made on an unreproduced flake is a guess. The coordinator decides
   whether to run V3's five-run tripwire as the base instead — that is a
   coordinator call, not a silent substitution.
2. **The fix needs `workers: 1`, or anything in `e2e/playwright.config.ts`.**
   Stop and report. The pass condition is default workers; a config change hides
   the isolation bug instead of fixing it and makes every later row slower.
   (Must not edit, Fixed decision 2.)
3. **The formats count cannot be scoped without losing an assertion.** Stop and
   report the exact assertion and what it would take. Replacing
   `toHaveLength(before + 1)` with `toBeGreaterThan`, deleting it, or `test.skip`
   are all masking, not fixing (Fixed decision 2, 3). Nor is Fixed decision 2's
   `--repeat-each=1` exclusion for `formats.spec.ts` this stop: that is a
   scheduling choice, and it buys nothing if the count was weakened.
4. **`plan.spec.ts` fails for a reason its own code does not explain, or you
   cannot tell which assertion failed.** Stop and report the run's output
   excerpt. Note first that the review's second citation is not a test:
   `plan.spec.ts:21` is the doc comment at `:21-27` above `SPANISH_ATTESTATION`
   (`:28`), not a racing case, and the review itself did not capture the failing
   assertion (`S2.8-impl.md:95-97`). Fixing an uncaptured failure by reading
   around it is how a test stops being a promise.
5. **The fix looks like it needs production code** — a settings route that
   stops being global, a per-test database, a new API, a change to
   `server/src/db/settings.ts`'s merge. Stop and report why (HS-9). There is no
   product defect here.
6. **`docs/v2/evidence/P2.2/screenshots/` shows a diff after a run, or any May-edit
   path outside the six is needed.** For the screenshots, revert and continue —
   that is routine. For a seventh spec that writes the theme row or asserts a
   global count, stop and report the path and the line: AM-086 authorised this
   card's scope, and §6 reserves widening to the owner (Fixed decision 9).
7. **V1, V2, V3 or V4 fails in a file outside May edit** — including a prettier
   or ESLint failure on another session's in-flight file. Report it and re-run
   later; do not reformat or fix anything outside May edit. The card's own two
   required outputs are the one exception, because `prettier --check .` is run
   by `npm run lint` and covers them (it checks zero Markdown files —
   `.prettierignore` holds `*.md` — so in practice this means the `.ts` outputs
   if any). Every other file is the stop.

# Contract excerpts (authoritative)

## C-ISO@1 Isolation and the sandbox wrapper

**Built by** P0.3. **Proven by** P0.3 (negative tests) and Q1.1.
**Consumers:** every card that starts a server, opens a real database, runs
e2e, runs `check:format`/`check:refine`, runs a real-model eval or launches
the app.

**Interface** (`scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs`, Node, no dependencies):

| Command | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs run --port 7852 -- <cmd...>` | Creates run folder, starts server, verifies ownership, runs `<cmd>` with the sandbox environment, stops only what it started, exits with `<cmd>`'s code |
| `node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs env --port 7852` | Creates run folder only, prints `export` lines for tools that start their own server (Playwright) |
| `node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs selftest` | Runs the negative cases below; exit 0 only if all refuse correctly |

**Rules**
1. Run folder: `/tmp/apunta-v2/<runId>/` with `data/`, `logs/`, `tmp/`,
   mode `700`. `runId` = UTC timestamp + 8 random hex characters.
   `realpath` of every path must stay under `/tmp/apunta-v2/`; a symlink that
   escapes is refused.
2. Port must be an integer 7800 to 7889 and free (checked by binding, then
   released immediately before the server binds). 7717 is always refused.
   7890 to 7899 are reserved for the updater test server (C-UPD) and refused
   here.
3. The data folder is never the platform default. The wrapper computes the
   default with `platformDataDir()` (C-PATH) **as a string only** and refuses
   if the sandbox path equals it or is inside it. It never lists or opens the
   default.
4. Server environment: `APUNTA_DATA_DIR`, `APUNTA_PORT`, `APUNTA_NO_OPEN=1`,
   `APUNTA_TEST_RUN_ID=<runId>`, `APUNTA_V2=1`. When `APUNTA_TEST_RUN_ID` is
   set, `/api/health` includes `"testRunId"`; the field never appears
   otherwise.
5. Ownership check: the wrapper polls `/api/health` for up to 30 s and
   proceeds only if `testRunId` equals its `runId`. Anything else (no
   answer, a different id, no id) is refused and the child is stopped.
6. Child command environment adds `APUNTA_CHECK_URL`, `APUNTA_E2E_PORT`,
   `APUNTA_V2=1`.
7. Cleanup kills only the process group the wrapper created. Never `pkill`,
   never the Ollama daemon.
8. When `APUNTA_V2=1`: Playwright sets `reuseExistingServer: false`;
   `scripts/check-note-format.mjs` and `scripts/check-refine.mjs` exit 2 if
   `APUNTA_CHECK_URL` is unset or points at port 7717.

**Normal example.** `sandbox.mjs run --port 7801 -- npm run check:format`
→ run folder created, server answers with the matching `testRunId`, the
check runs against `http://127.0.0.1:7801`, server stopped, exit code of the
check.

**Rejection examples** (each must be a `selftest` case, refused before any
database is opened): `--port 7717`; `--port 7890`; port in use by a dummy
listener; a dummy server on the port answering `/api/health` with 200 but no
or wrong `testRunId`; run folder symlinked outside `/tmp/apunta-v2/`;
`APUNTA_DATA_DIR` equal to the platform default string.

## C-SETTINGS@1 Settings mutations

**Built by** P1.1. **Proven by** P1.1 and S2.6. **Consumers:** every
settings control, including Language.

- `SettingsProvider` exposes `update(patch)`. It applies the patch to the
  provider's state immediately (optimistic), then calls `putSettings`.
- Each key has a sequence number. A response for an older sequence than the
  latest request for that key is ignored (last intent wins).
- On failure: the provider restores the value from before **that** request
  for the failed keys only, and the control shows the existing error
  message style.
- No control keeps a persisted setting in local component state as its
  source of truth. Local state is allowed only for in-progress text input.
- Radio groups follow native radio keyboard behaviour: arrow keys move and
  select within the group; Tab enters at the selected option.

**Normal example.** Dark → choose Light → navigate to Home → back to
Settings **without reload** → Light selected, page light, provider value
light; after reload, still light.

**Rejection example.** Save fails → value returns to Dark, page returns to
dark, error shown; no reload claims Light.

# Run configuration (v2 plan)

## 1. Ports

| Use | Port |
| --- | --- |
| Live instance: **never contact** | 7717 |
| Sandbox servers (C-ISO) | 7800 to 7889 |
| Updater test server (C-UPD) | 7890 to 7899 |
| Playwright under the sandbox | the port `sandbox.mjs env` assigns |

## 2. Gate levels

A card names one level. Commands run from the repository root unless a card
says otherwise. Until P0.3 is APPROVED, only L0 and the non-launching part of
L1 may run.

| Level | When | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **L0** docs only | cards that change only Markdown | `npx prettier --check <changed files>`; `node scripts/check-no-external-urls.mjs` |
| **L1** targeted | every implementation card | `npm run lint`; `npm run typecheck`; `npm run build:shared`, then the card's named test files with `npx vitest run <paths>` from the repository root (the root `vitest.config.ts` defines the projects) |
| **L2** parent acceptance | every parent review card | everything in §3 |
| **L3** native or real model | cards and parent reviews that say so | the card's listed commands, all through `sandbox.mjs` |

## 3. The L2 suite

```sh
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
TZ=UTC npm test
TZ=America/Denver npm test
TZ=America/Mexico_City npm test
TZ=Australia/Sydney npm test
npm run build
node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs env --port 7810 > /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && . /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && npm run e2e
npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1
```

After P0.2, each `TZ=` run prints its effective zone (a test asserts it), so
four runs really exercise four zones. After P0.3, the e2e line is the only
permitted way to run Playwright. After S3.2, add
`npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1 --corpus e2e/fixtures/eval-es/tuning`.
After P3.3, add `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and
`cargo test` in `src-tauri/`.

## 4. Evidence

- Write detailed output to `docs/v2/evidence/<card-id>/`. Keep it sanitized:
  replace sandbox paths with `<sandbox>`, the home folder with `~`, and never
  include hostnames, usernames, keys, tokens or real names.
- Raw logs stay in the sandbox run folder and are never committed.
- Each command's evidence records: working directory, exact command, exit
  code, start and end time, and a short excerpt (failures in full, up to 200
  lines).
- Status words: criteria `NOT RUN`, `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`; cards
  `NOT STARTED`, `IN PROGRESS`, `SUBMITTED`, `APPROVED`,
  `CHANGES REQUESTED`, `BLOCKED`; instruction reviews `CLEAR`, `DEFECT`,
  `UNKNOWN`. Every blank template starts at `NOT RUN` or `UNKNOWN`.

**Redirect admission (rule 1).** A redirect is followed only when its `Location`
resolves to `https:`, port 443, no user-info, no fragment, a host the row's
*Redirect hosts* cell admits, and a query whose every parameter name appears in
that row's *Allowed query keys* cell. A parameter name outside the cell is
refused (`query_key_not_allowed`) before the URL is requested. `none` means the
row admits no query at all, so any query is `query_not_allowed` — that is the
default and it is unchanged. No row admits a query by wildcard, a prefix or a
blanket permission, and the cell is the complete list: adding a name is a
plan-editor amendment (AM-042).

**Why A07's names are safe to enumerate.** The ten names are the AWS
CloudFront signed-URL parameter set plus Hugging Face's Xet and
`response-content-*` parameters, observed on 2026-09-26 across all six C-STT
artifacts and the one speech artifact, each answering `302` to
`us.aws.cdn.hf.co` (`docs/v2/evidence/P4.1/redirects.md`). They cannot change
*which* bytes arrive: the path is fixed by the pinned catalogue URL and the
bytes are verified against the pinned `sha256`, and the committed name is the
entry's own `sizeBytes` path, so the two `response-content-*` parameters can
only shape headers a client would have sent anyway. The card's own worry — "a
query string is where a download URL turns into a message" — is about
*outbound* data, and none of these names carries any: the probe records the
**names** only and writes every value as `<redacted>`, so a signature is never
in the repository, the evidence or any log.

**The four-arm comparison (A13, A14, A15).** Added 2026-09-26 on the owner's
approval, for one measurement round and nothing else. The arms are
`qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` as the control (A08; already present, and A08's "never pulled
if present" still holds), plus A13, A14 and A15. Three rules bind the round and
are not negotiable per run:

1. **No candidate becomes a default.** A07's "selected one only" and A08's tag
   are unchanged. The round measures; it does not promote.
2. **The licence of A14 and A15 is unknown to the coordinator and must be found
   before either is pulled.** These are models downloaded by the user at setup,
   so L-POLICY@1's row for that applies: per the publisher's licence, shown and
   recorded. Prism's licence for these repositories is not asserted here because
   it was not verified — anyone pulling them records the licence text and the
   URL it came from, or reports `BLOCKED`. Guessing it is exactly the failure
   this manifest exists to prevent.
3. **The GPU is not shared.** One model loaded at a time, `keep_alive` set so
   each unloads after its arm, and no arm runs while the owner is testing on the
   machine or a live instance is in use. A four-arm run is long and real.

**Fraunces (A16) follows Kalam, not a build-time download.** Both source TTFs live in `docs/v2/assets/` with their OFL texts, and `build-brand-fraunces.py` reads the local file and touches no network — regenerating the wordmark in six years must not depend on a `/tmp` file or a download working. A16 permits exactly that one fetch, to obtain the file committed beside it. Fraunces is a **variable** font; the committed cut is the variable one, and the generator pins `wght 500`, `opsz 14`, `SOFT 0`, `WONK 0`, because a static instance could not set optical size and an unpinned variable font would not reproduce. The TTF is never bundled: the app ships outlines only.

**Owner-run items.** `apt` needs `sudo`. The coordinator writes the exact
command to `docs/v2/state/OWNER-ACTIONS.md`, stops the dependent cards, and
waits; the owner runs it. Agents never enter a password.

**Ollama.** Before any pull, run `ollama list`; if the tag exists, do not pull.
Record the digest with `ollama show <tag>`. Real-model runs set Ollama's
`keep_alive` so evaluation models unload after use, and run only one model
at a time, to avoid starving the live instance.

## 2. Development tools already present

Anything already installed on the PC (git, Python, Piper if present,
whisper-cli, Ollama) may be used as found. Record its version in evidence.

## 3. L-POLICY@1 Licences

One rule, applied per object reviewed (a tool, a library, a model file, a
voice, a dictionary, generated audio are separate objects).

| Object | Allowed |
| --- | --- |
| Code or data **shipped** in the app or installer | MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC, Zlib, 0BSD, Unicode, OFL-1.1 (fonts), CC0, CC-BY-4.0 (data, with attribution) |
| The one pre-approved exception | Spanish dictionary **data** under an MPL option of a multi-licence, shipped unmodified in its own files, election and obligations stated in `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md` and `docs/decisions.md` |
| Development-only tools never shipped or linked | any OSI licence, including GPL (Piper) |
| Generated fixtures committed to the repo | only if the voice's model card permits redistribution of generated audio; otherwise generate at test time into the sandbox and never commit |
| Models downloaded by the user at setup | per the publisher's licence, shown in setup, recorded in the catalogue |
| System libraries bundled into an AppImage (for example WebKitGTK, LGPL) | allowed for **test builds**; **public distribution requires owner review** (listed in the final report) |

Anything else: do not add it; the card reports `BLOCKED` with the licence
text found. A dependency's MIT wrapper does not change its data's licence.
